newsitem.title: USA: Fed taking out insurance via mkt rate rise - Angell.
newsitem.headline: Fed taking out insurance via mkt rate rise - Angell.

text.p: Former Federal Reserve Board Governor Wayne Angell said on Tuesday he believes the U.S. central bank was taking out insurance against inflationary pressures by allowing market interest rates to rise recently.
"I think the Fed is taking out insurance by letting rates run up," Angell told reporters during a European Institute confernece here.
Angell is currently chief economist and senior managing director at Bear Stearns & Co.
Market interest rates had risen earlier in the year but on Tuesday weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data sparked a rally in the U.S. Treasury market that caused interest rates to fall.
Angell also told reporters that the Fed may tighten credit again this year.

"And, I think we might expect...he (Fed chairman Alan Greenspan) might buy insurance one more time this year, but I've held that not necessarily at the May 20 meeting as the markets are presupposing," Angell said.
The Fed's policy-setting arm, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), voted to hike the key overnight lending rate by a 1/4 point on March 25.
Policy-makers are set to meet again on May 20.
